nodes.name: Catalytic Polymerization-Ion Reduction
nodes.procedure: A methanol solution containing Fe³⁺, Ru³⁺, and pyrrole monomers is utilized. Polypyrrole (PPy) is produced through the oxidative polymerization of pyrrole monomer (Py) with Fe³⁺ serving as the oxidizing agent. During the polymerization process, Fe ions are incorporated into the PPy network to maintain electrical neutrality. Additionally, external Ru³⁺ ions and residual Fe³⁺ ions can be reduced by electrons from the conductive network, leading to the formation of metallic species. Some radicals such as hydroxide may further improve the reducing capacity of PPy. Fe³⁺ are the main ions that catalyze the polymerization of Py and participate in the coordination.

nodes.name: High-temperature Annealing
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, annealing at a high temperature in an inert atmosphere results in the formation of the RuFe/FeNC catalyst. The Fe single-atom control catalyst (FeNC), which also serves as the support for the Ru/FeNC control catalyst, was synthesized using the same procedure (see the Experimental section for details; Fig. S7, ESI†). The coordination number of isolated Fe sites within the defective carbon matrix was determined to be approximately 4, indicating the formation of an Fe-N4 configuration at high temperature.

nodes.description: HER performance in Ar-saturated 1.0 M KOH aqueous solution
nodes.source_text: The HER activity of RuFe/FeNC and control catalysts was evaluated in Ar-saturated 1.0 M KOH aqueous solution ... RuFe/FeNC achieved a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} at an overpotential of 9.3 mV (vs. V_{RHE}) ... small Tafel slope of 20.4 mV decade^{-1} ... RuFe/FeNC exhibited a remarkable mass activity exceeding 1600 A g^{-1} at the same potential ... normalized current density of RuFe/FeNC was ... 0.997 mA cm^{-2} at -0.02 V_{RHE} ... TOF value of 1.35 H_2 s^{-1} ... Chronoamperometry measurements were conducted over 40 hours at a potential of -0.01 V_{RHE}, and the current density showed only a negligible decline ... LSV curves of RuFe/FeNC showed only a slight increase in the overpotential of 2.0 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC exhibit five diffraction peaks at 38.8°, 42.5°, 44.4°, 58.7°, and 69.9° corresponding to (100), (002), (101), (102), and (110) planes of hexagonal Ru crystal. Broad peak at 26° corresponds to (002) plane of graphitic arrays.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC exhibited five diffraction peaks at approximately 38.8°, 42.5°, 44.4°, 58.7°, and 69.9°, corresponding well with the planes of (100), (002), (101), (102), and (110) of hexagonal Ru crystal ... The broad diffraction peaks at about 26° observed for both RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC corresponded to the (002) plane of the graphitic arrays.

properties.description: TEM image with diffraction pattern inset

nodes.characterization_summary: RuFe/FeNC shows uniformly dispersed fine nanoparticles on defective carbon matrix with (001) indexed hexagonal structure exposing (001) surface. Elemental mapping shows uniform Fe distribution and Ru mainly in nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) image of RuFe/FeNC revealed uniformly dispersed fine nanoparticles on the defective carbon matrix ... Elemental mapping analysis indicated a uniform distribution of Fe in RuFe/FeNC, while Ru signals mainly appeared at the position of nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in RuFe/FeNC is 7.1 wt% and in Ru/FeNC is 15.3 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The total Ru contents in RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC were about 7.1 wt% and 15.3 wt%, respectively, as determined by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS of RuFe/FeNC shows prominent peak at 2.41 Å (Ru-Ru path) resembling Ru foil, indicating metallic Ru nature. Fe K-edge shows peaks at 1.51 Å (Fe-N path) and 2.38 Å (Fe-Ru path).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru K-edge Fourier transform extended XAFS (FT-EXAFS) spectrum of RuFe/FeNC exhibited a prominent peak at approximately 2.41 Å, closely resembling that of Ru foil ... Thus, this peak is attributed to the Ru–Ru path of metallic Ru ... the Fe K-edge FT-EXAFS of RuFe/FeNC exhibited two primary peaks at approximately 1.51 and 2.38 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: Isolated metal atoms confirmed on defective carbon substrate in all samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field STEM (HAADF-STEM) observation confirmed the presence of isolated metal atoms on the defective carbon substrate in all samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p and Fe 2p XPS spectra of pristine and spent RuFe/FeNC show no significant differences, indicating structural preservation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To assess the structural stability, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was conducted on RuFe/FeNC. The Ru 3p and Fe 2p XPS spectra of both pristine and spent RuFe/FeNC exhibited no significant differences.

nodes.characterization_summary: RuFe/FeNC shows stronger O-H stretching band indicating greater water adsorption capacity than Ru/FeNC. Higher population of 1H-down interfacial water molecules compared to Ru/FeNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A broad Raman band stemming from the O–H stretching mode of H2O was observed ... the RuFe/FeNC system exhibited a larger population of H-down water, thereby highlighting a difference in the distribution of interfacial water between RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peak at 1061 cm⁻¹ assigned to hydroxide adsorption on Fe sites. Peak at 1752 cm⁻¹ assigned to hydronium indicating acid-like microenvironment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3(h) presents an obvious peak located at around 1061 cm⁻¹. This peak was assigned to the hydroxide adsorption on Fe sites ... In Fig. 3(i), a peak at around 1752 cm⁻¹ was assigned to the hydronium.
